chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And that to your Lord is the end of all.' He said: 'If the statement ends with Allah, the Mighty and High, then abstain.'
ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'And to your Lord is the end' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the verse 'And to your Lord is the end' as a specific injunction to remain silent when theological discourse reaches the limits of human comprehension, marking the boundary of divine knowledge. This highlights the Shia principle of *tafwid* (assigning the ultimate reality to God) in attributes, warning against excessive speculation (*ta'til*) that leads to error. The directive to 'cease speech' underscores the reverence due to the unseen (*ghayb*) and the importance of epistemic humility in creedal matters.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 9. And with the same chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Khalid

that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to interpret the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And that to your Lord is the end of all. He said: “If the statement ends with Allah, the Mighty and High, then abstain.”
